Yes. The Bot API, the Telegram API (MTProto) and TDLib are free. Telegram does not charge for a bot token, for requests or for the number of users.

title: Is the Telegram Bot API Free? Official Pricing, Fees & Limits (2026)
snippet:
**Quick answer: Yes, the Telegram Bot API is free.** Telegram charges no fees to create a bot, call the API or send messages — there are no paid tiers and no per-message costs, and the official Bot API documentation lists no pricing. Your only costs are running the bot (hosting, database) and optional extras like [Telegram Stars](https://aziqdev.com/blog/telegram-stars-explained) payments and paid broadcasts. The API does have [rate limits](https://aziqdev.com/blog/telegram-bot-api-rate-limits) — about 30 messages per second overall and 1 per second per chat.
The Telegram Bot API is completely free. No monthly fee, no per-request charge, no paid tier upgrade. But if you search for "Telegram bot API pricing" and expect a simple answer, you will find the question is more nuanced: **the API is free, but running a production bot has real ongoing costs** — and those costs catch many builders off guard.

FREE
### Telegram Bot API
$0/month
The Bot API gives your bot the ability to send messages, receive updates, manage groups, handle payments, serve inline queries, and interact with Telegram's full feature set. There is no paid plan, no API key pricing tier, and no per-message fee.
**Rate limits (not paid, just enforced):**
- 30 messages per second to different users
- 20 messages per minute to the same group
- No documented limit on incoming updates
These limits are soft throttles, not hard paywalls. You cannot pay to increase them. Design your bot to respect them.

## Free Hosting Options (With Trade-offs)
Several platforms offer free tiers that work for development and low-traffic bots:
- **Railway (free tier):** 500 free hours/month — enough for a bot running 16 hours/day. $5/month for always-on.
- **Render (free tier):** Free web services that spin down after 15 minutes of inactivity. Polling bots work; webhook bots spin down between messages. Fine for personal projects.
- **Fly.io (free tier):** 3 shared VMs free. Better for always-on bots than Render.
- **Oracle Cloud Free Tier:** Permanently free ARM VMs (2 vCPU, 12 GB RAM). Best free production option — no credit card spin-down issues.

title: Is the Telegram API Free? The Real Cost Explained – Unipile
snippet:
Yes, the Telegram Bot API and the Telegram API (MTProto) are both free to use, with no per-message fee and no pricing tier. But free access isn't the same as free to run.

Both API surfaces you would use to build on Telegram, the Bot API and the Telegram API (MTProto), are free to use. There is no message quota, no per-message fee and no pricing tier tied to volume. That settles the Telegram API price question. It does not settle the cost question, which is a different thing and the actual subject of this article.
The Telegram API is free. No message-based pricing, no tier, no quota.
Telegram states both the Bot API and the Telegram API are usable free of charge. The Bot API is currently at version 10.2, published July 14, 2026. Free access is not the full story: the infrastructure, the ban risk, and the implementation time behind that access are where the real cost sits, and they're covered in the sections below.

Telegram exposes three distinct API surfaces plus one consumer subscription. Only two of the four are free for developers. Confusing them is where most "is the Telegram API free" questions actually come from.
Bot APIFree
HTTP interface for bot accounts, created through `BotFather`. Telegram states it is usable free of charge. Currently at version 10.2, published July 14, 2026. No message quota, no billing tier.
Telegram API (MTProto)Free
The protocol behind full Telegram clients, also free to use. Requires an `api_id` and `api_hash` obtained on `my.telegram.org`, one `api_id` per phone number.
Gateway APIPaid
Sends one-time verification codes for account authentication. A separate product from the Bot API and the Telegram API, billed per verification. Out of scope for this article: it isn't a messaging API.
Telegram PremiumPaid
A consumer subscription for end users (larger uploads, reactions, badges). It sits on the user side of the app, not on the developer side, and has no bearing on whether an API integration is billed.

title: Telegram Bot API pricing: what is free and what still costs money
snippet:
## Short answer: normal Bot API access is free
Telegram describes its Bot Platform as free for users and developers. You create a bot account with BotFather and connect your own program to Telegram's HTTP Bot API. Telegram does not charge a monthly API subscription for ordinary bot requests.
That does not mean a production bot has no cost. Telegram hosts the messaging platform, but your code, database, integrations, logs, backups, support process, and any paid third-party services still need an owner and usually need infrastructure.

| Cost area | Simple planning range | What changes it |
|---|---|---|
| Telegram Bot API | $0 for ordinary use | Paid high-speed broadcasts are a separate case. |
| Small bot hosting | $0–$25/month | Sleep limits, uptime, memory, region, backups, and traffic. |
| Database and storage | $0–$25/month initially | Record count, media, backups, retention, and compliance needs. |
| Development | One-time project cost | Conversation branches, validation, admin tools, roles, and testing. |
| External integrations | Variable | CRM, calendar, payment, spreadsheet, email, or private API fees. |
| AI model usage | Usage-based | Model, prompt size, response length, retrieval, and monthly volume. |
| Monitoring and maintenance | Time or monthly support | Uptime expectations, incident response, vendor changes, and content updates. |

title: Is the Telegram Bot API free? Pricing and limits
snippet:
Yes, the Telegram Bot API is free. Telegram’s documentation says the Bot Platform “is free for both users and developers”, and by default bots message their users at no cost. There is no subscription and no fee per request. The one charge the docs describe is optional: paid broadcasts, at 0.1 Telegram Stars for each message sent above the free 30 messages per second. Everything else a bot costs, such as a server, a database and outside services, is paid to other companies.

Yes. Telegram’s introduction to bots says the Bot Platform “is free for both users and developers”, and the Bots FAQ adds that by default bots message their users “at no cost”. The documentation doesn’t describe a paid plan or a price per request.
Two things can still cost money:
- **Paid broadcasts, if you choose them.** A bot that must send bulk messages faster than about 30 per second can pay 0.1 Telegram Stars for each message above the free amount.
- **Everything around the API.** A server, a database and third-party services are billed by other companies, not by Telegram.

“Telegram bot API free of charge” covers more than sending text. In the documentation none of the following has a price:
- **Creating a bot.** You register it with @BotFather and receive its token. No phone number is needed.
- **Sending messages.** Private chats, groups and channels, within the limits in the next section.
- **Receiving updates** through long polling or webhooks.
- **Files:** sending and downloading within the size limits.
- **The payments platform.** Telegram calls Bot Payments “a free and open platform”.
- **The Bot API server itself.** Its source code is published, and you may run your own copy.

| Limit | Value | Source page |
|---|---|---|
| Messages in a single chat | Avoid more than one per second; short bursts may be allowed | Bots FAQ |
| Messages in a group | No more than 20 per minute | Bots FAQ |
| Bulk notifications | About 30 messages per second | Bots FAQ, Bot API |
| Downloading a file | Up to 20 MB | Bots FAQ, Bot API |
| Uploading a new file | 10 MB for photos, 50 MB for other files | Bot API |
| Sending a file by URL | 5 MB for photos, 20 MB for other content | Bot API |
| Resending a file by file_id | No limits | Bot API |

The only price for sending messages in the Bot API documentation is for paid broadcasts. By default every bot can broadcast up to 30 messages per second. With Paid Broadcasts enabled in @BotFather, the limit rises to 1000 messages per second.
